schema_note: Summary of the S&P 500 stock layer (Plan 5, phase P3) after the final-review fix wave; no price data. Paths are relative to the data root unless stated. Dataset n1 and its derived files are superseded history and stay in the data root.

labels_carried_by.tearsheet_title: yes, from the fix wave (code commit 4d6500e)
labels_carried_by.run_manifests: labels and universe_kind keys in every stock-class or membership-masked run manifest (analysis ladder and both parity engines) from the fix wave; ETF run manifests keep exactly their old keys
labels_carried_by.correction: the first version of this record said every stock analysis and receipt carried the labels; run manifests and the tearsheet did not. Runs written before the fix wave (including the n1 runs) have no labels in their manifests; their datasets block carries universe_kind

survivor_bias_statement: The universe is the issuer's current SPY equity holdings (a current-holdings proxy). Former members' prices are out of scope, so the dataset cannot represent names that left the index. Point-in-time membership masks the proxy names by date but cannot add the missing names. Share of S&P 500 members with data per date: minimum 0.5714 (2016-01-04, 288 of 504), median 0.6990, 0.7932 on 2025-12-31 (399 of 503). Results are discovery-only and cannot clear G2.

dataset.cache: keyed on the manifest hash and a code version (hash of etf_normalise.py and market_model.py); a cache from other code is rebuilt

actions.dividend_unadjustment: each Yahoo amount multiplied by the product of the ratios of that symbol's in-window splits dated after the ex-date
actions.pay_date: not provided; pay_date = ex_date, credited on the ex-date (pay_date_unknown_credited_on_ex_date)
actions.excluded_reason: any split that is not an integer forward ratio >= 2 (reverse or non-integer) excludes the symbol; most of these are spin-off or merger adjustments that Yahoo encodes as ratios near 1 (for example 1.046:1 for IBM), not stock splits

post_window_adjustment.finding: Yahoo closes and dividends for some symbols are adjusted for splits or spin-offs after the window end, which the raw archive prices are not; un-adjusting dividends for in-window splits does not remove that adjustment
post_window_adjustment.rule: exclude a symbol whose median Alpaca close over Yahoo close (Yahoo closes first un-adjusted for its own in-window splits) over the last 20 window sessions differs from 1 by more than 0.005; no factor is inferred

actions.disclosure: Large caps are missing from the stock dataset because of the exclusion rule, so the dataset is not representative of the index's largest names.

quality_report_summary.gaps_on_split_dates: split_consistency passes for all 60 split records (raw close times ratio within 15 percent of the previous close); the 165 gaps are real moves above 25 percent on non-split days
quality_report_summary.cross_source_note: Alpaca vs Yahoo: 1,024,531 compared, 3,695 not compared, 3,906 breaches (21,504 on n1 before the post-window exclusion); 368 symbols have at least one; SW 2137, CBOE 379, SMCI 353 and IBKR 122 account for 2991; listed, not resolved

membership.source: fja05680/sp500, S&P 500 Historical Components & Changes (Updated).csv, MIT licence text kept with the snapshot

spot_checks.name: FB present until 2022-06-08, META from 2022-06-09
spot_checks.note: the source carries two symbols; identity maps them to one issuer

cross_checks.dates: first trading day of each year 2016-2025

hanshof_sp500_constituents.note: current list only (as of 2025-08-23); names only there total 138 before identity resolution (n1 identity: 131) and 82 after the eight derived renames; 0 differences on 2025-08-23

unliftedq_index_constitution.note: differences are mostly ticker renames and the opt-out date convention; totals over the ten dates 198 primary-only and 177 other-only before identity resolution, 142 and 121 after; not tuned

identity.superseded: sp500-identity-20261118 (one ticker change applied; kept as history)

applied.origin: research/registry/ticker-changes.json, source_url null, verified false, note says no source could be checked offline

identity.derivation: derive-renames over the unresolved candidates of sp500-identity-20261118: new symbol in the dataset (159 candidates), old symbol historical-only, adjacent within 7 days, each symbol in one candidate on its side, old symbol a member in the window, and the current-members list (hanshof) dating the new symbol's addition more than 7 days before its first membership here. Records are verified false, source_url null, source_note 'derived from adjacent membership intervals in sp500-membership-20261118 (fja05680 file); not independently verified', with a corroboration field
identity.why_not_all_159: membership alone cannot tell a rename from a one-for-one replacement; applying all would merge unrelated companies (for example GLD to ADBE, TWTR to ACGL, AIV to TSLA) and widen the mask
identity.unverified: all nine ticker changes are unverified and need owner review before any G2 claim

cost_model.adv: median of close times volume over the 20 sessions strictly before the decision session; fewer than 20 sessions use the 25 bp tier
cost_model.convention: cost_bps(data, instrument, i, config) with i the decision session; the fill is at the open of i+1; raw close and raw volume; identical in both engines
cost_model.split_in_window: the first record said a split inside the window can distort ADV; that was wrong for this data: the Alpaca volume is raw (AAPL 2020-08-31 4:1 split: volume 244 million against 53 million the session before, close 129 against 499), so close times volume is split-invariant
cost_model.flat_unchanged: flat keeps the existing behaviour, hashes and goldens

performance.machine_note: Local machine shared with other sessions: load average 10 to 18 during every measurement, so timings are noisy. Same machine and dataset for before and after; single runs. Measured on n1 (416 names) before the fix wave.
optimisations: history_view slices per-instrument frames that carry split_factor, precomputed once per set of effective splits, instead of copying every frame each session
screening engine: splits and dividend pay dates looked up by date; session index map instead of list.index
native engine: bar columns read from arrays instead of per-row iloc; dividend ex and pay dates looked up by date; session index maps

native_416_adv_extrapolated_seconds.method: native seconds for 20 names multiplied by 416/20 (linear in names; not measured on 416)

performance.target: screening all names under 5 minutes: met before and after
performance.remaining_cost: most of the remaining screening time is pandas work inside the strategy callback, not the engine; native time is mostly NautilusTrader itself

bit_identity.method: pandas row hashes of the returns, positions, signals and fills tables plus the cash series, same data and strategy before and after
bit_identity.incumbent_spec_rebuild: scripts/analysis.py run with research/registry/analysis-specs/incumbent-spy-gate.json in two temp roots, HEAD before the change and after: 16 run table files identical, analysis.json identical after normalising ids and timestamps
bit_identity.guard_test: tests/current/test_market_model.py::HistoryViewTests::test_history_view_matches_reference compares the view with a copy of the original construction at every session of the fixture, two split ratios
bit_identity.golden: make golden-check passed unchanged, also after the fix wave

parity.instruments: first 20 symbols alphabetically (A through ALB); includes AFL 2:1, ACGL 3:1 and AAPL 4:1 splits and 632 dividends
parity.scope: engineering evidence on 20 of 409 names; says nothing about the other names or about financial results
